problem: Prior VLN work focuses on data augmentation and new losses, ignoring depth as a signal; models also lack the ability to capture directions relative to the grounding view, and suffer a large domain gap between seen and unseen environments.
motivation: VLN is a spatial and temporal search task in which depth is a valuable but unexploited cue. A large seen/unseen domain gap hurts generalization, and depth features may help make RGB features environment-adaptive. Modeling relative direction in attention is also needed to follow directional instructions.
key_idea: Use a Depth-Guided AdaIN (DG-AdaIN) module to modulate RGB features with depth features for environment adaptation, and a shift attention module to encode relative direction information in the attention map.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract claims that conditioning RGB feature statistics on depth reduces the seen/unseen domain gap, and that shifting attention relative to the grounding view supplies directional awareness.
method: DG-AdaIN: Depth-guided Adaptive Instance Normalization that adjusts RGB visual features according to depth features, for environment adaptation.
Shift attention module: models relative direction information in the attention map, relative to the grounding view.
